summary: Instagram is carrying the channel: most videos get 1,000+ views there, while YouTube Shorts mostly get under 60 views. The best performers are surprising 'this thing doesn't do what you think' videos about robots and clap switches, and the ones that get shared or saved are the most useful. Many near-identical topics (smoke detectors, automatic taps, IR sensors) are repeating and getting weak results, and a few videos were never posted to Instagram at all.
winningPattern: Instagram Reels in Hindi about a single relatable gadget (robot, clap switch, mic, line follower, DHT11), with a 'It doesn't do X, it only does Y' or 'Without Z it falls' hook. Short Hinglish titles with one emoji and a curiosity gap work best. Robot and clap-switch videos lead on YouTube too. Videos with a visible demo or surprising behavior get the shares and saves.
doMore: Post every video on Instagram too: 5 of the last 30 have zero Instagram numbers
Use the 'doesn't do X, only does Y' contrast hook, which drove the top videos
Make robot and clap-switch follow-ups, since both topics worked on both platforms
Open with a visible demo or failure moment in the first second
End with a save-worthy takeaway such as a wiring tip or one-line rule to boost saves and shares
stopDoing: Repeating the same sensor topic in near-identical videos (3 smoke, 3 tap, 3 IR) with different titles
Plain 'How does X work?' titles with no surprise, which scored lowest
Posting English narration on a Hindi channel
